    - Leland. Well-digger, or I was, until my knees retired before I did. You will be wondering why an old man stands in a kitchen passage staring at a door. Everybody does. Mags has stopped asking and started bringing me stew.
    - The Table said yes, I hear. Opened in one night, they say upstairs, and nobody can believe it. Well, the door has not heard. Hex will have to tell it. I am going to stand right here while that happens.
    - Keeper of the Low Door. They gave me the title, a lamp, and a coil of new rope from Rivet. I gave myself the chalk. Going down, *Player*?
    - Undercroft, Floodwells, Deep Roads, Warm Quarry. All four on the wall in chalk, thanks to you. Mapped, not understood. Still: mapped. Going down again?
    - What can an old well-digger tell you?
        - *Choice:* What is behind that door?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about digging wells.
        - *Choice:* What is under the city?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Down, or a word first?
        - *Choice:* Take me down into Low Grad.
        - *Choice:* Open the way to the Warmstone Colossus.
        - *Choice:* Show me your chalk map.
        - *Choice:* What is under the city?
        - *Choice:* Nothing, thanks.
    - Nobody knows. The Walkers found it locked when they patched this hall, and they had roofs to mend and plays to put on, so they left it. A hundred years, everyone has walked past it to get to the stew.
    - I have put my ear to it. I hear air moving, and water, a long way down. That is all I will say about what I hear. A well-digger who guesses out loud ends up digging in the wrong place.
    - Sixty years of them, all over the city. Yards, cellars, under a bakery once; the baker brought me a loaf a day until I struck water. You learn to read stone by the sound your pick makes. Dull is earth. Bright is rock. Hollow is trouble.
    - Under this city, the pick rings hollow more often than you would like. There are rooms down there nobody has lived in since the Aristocrats left. I have broken into two by accident. I bricked them up and said nothing. I am saying something now.
    - Old Grad was a fortress before it was a city. A fortress digs: cellars for its stores, cisterns for its water, tunnels so its soldiers could get in and out without the gate. The Walkers built their city on top of all that and painted it bright.
    - The bright part is real. So is the part underneath. I have always thought somebody ought to know both. It seems that somebody is me.
    - Rope's tied. Lamp low. Mind the third step; it is not a step. I will be right here at the top.
    - Not yet. I have seen what crawls along those shelves, and you are not ready for it. Come back when you have a few more scars from the Outworks, around level **20**. I mean that kindly.
    - To the Warm Quarry's heart, then. Potions. Mind the glowing floor. And come back up.
    - Here, on the kitchen wall: Mags allows it as long as I do not chalk over the soup list. Top to bottom, as far as anyone has gone. Every stair, every walkway, every place the floor is not a floor.
    - Where I have not been, I draw a question mark. There are fewer question marks every week. There are still a lot of them.
    - Go well. Up here or down there.
